footerNote: All figures are GAAP, in $ millions unless noted; EPS is shown exactly as reported in the release — GAAP diluted EPS of $2.84 — on a pre-split basis. Free cash flow is cash from operations of $4,815M less $122M of capital expenditures. Net income of $1,325M includes $51M from discontinued operations; continuing operations earned $1,274M, and the $51M is folded into otherIncomeM so the flow balances to total net income, following the Q4 FY24 sibling precedent. The tax provision was just $68M — there was no large one-time intra-group IP-transfer tax charge this quarter.

oneTimers: GAAP profit carries $2,172M of amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets ($1,380M inside cost of revenue and $792M inside operating expenses) — mostly bookkeeping from the VMware deal, not cash. On Broadcom's non-GAAP view, net income was $5,254M instead of $1,325M.

Restructuring charges totaled $712M ($92M inside cost of revenue and $620M inside operating expenses), primarily employee termination costs from integrating VMware, and the non-GAAP reconciliation also adds back $292M of acquisition-related costs.

Stock-based compensation expense was $1,572M, up from $391M a year ago, including a one-time impact from aligning the vesting dates of equity awards assumed in the VMware merger and accelerated vesting for employees terminated in connection with the merger.

Discontinued operations added $51M, net of tax — mainly VMware's end-user computing business held for sale, which Broadcom agreed in February 2024 to sell for approximately $3.8B. Profit from continuing operations was $1,274M.
otherDetail: Interest expense of $926M on Broadcom's debt, much of it taken on to buy VMware, partly offset by $185M of other income, net — interest income, investment gains/losses and other items — plus $51M of profit from discontinued operations folded in here, for a net -$690M below operating profit.

segments.note: Chips — above all networking products for AI data centers and custom AI accelerators from hyperscalers. Strong networking demand was partly offset by lower demand for server storage and broadband products.

segments.name: Infrastructure software

takeaways.text: Infrastructure software revenue rose 153% to $4.6B — 38% of all revenue, up from 20% a year ago — in VMware's first full quarter, making Broadcom nearly as much a software company as a chip company.
takeaways.title: VMware transformed the mix

takeaways.text: GAAP net income fell to $1,325M from $3,774M a year ago despite revenue rising 34%, weighed down by $2,172M of acquisition amortization, $712M of restructuring charges and $1,572M of stock-based compensation. On Broadcom's non-GAAP view, net income was $5,254M.
takeaways.title: Profit fell even as sales soared

takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $4,693M — 39% of revenue — from $4,815M of cash from operations less $122M of capital expenditures. Excluding restructuring in the quarter, management put free cash flow at $5.4B.
takeaways.title: Cash flow stayed strong

verdict: Broadcom's revenue jumped 34% to $12.0B in VMware's first full quarter — software surged 153% and AI networking demand grew — but the cost of absorbing VMware cut GAAP profit to $1.3B.
